headline: AI selloff pauses into a thin half-day; Dec hike priced, VXN 38.53

what_happened.summary: Stocks opened deep in the red on 25 Nov, led by Nvidia, then dip buyers pulled them well off the lows. The Nasdaq-100 briefly touched bear-market territory intraday and closed at 26046.9 (-0.64%). The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.21%, went below 7,000 and closed at 7182.78 (-0.25%). The Dow closed 0.33% higher on defensive rotation. US markets were closed on 26 Nov, and today's half-day session is expected to be thin.
what_happened.market_action: VXN closed at 38.53 and VIX at 28.29 on 25 Nov. COR1M was 25.45, well below 36.05 on 20 Nov. VIX was 26.8 (-5.27%) in the 26 Nov data print. The Nasdaq-100 minus S&P 500 gap was -0.38 pct pts on 25 Nov and -2.02 pct pts over five sessions.
what_happened.macro: Core PCE was 3.26% y/y and 0.29% m/m for October, headline PCE 3.84% y/y. The 10-year yield fell 6.0 bp to 4.85% and the 2-year to 4.61% on 25 Nov. A 25 bp December hike is priced at 94.5% (Polymarket). The January hike probability is 59% on CME FedWatch, down from 70% a week earlier.
what_happened.geopolitics: Not covered by the sources. Official oil data is stale to 24 Nov: Brent 91.8 $/bbl, WTI 82.24 $/bbl.
what_happened.company_news: S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia's senior unsecured debt on CreditWatch negative, citing management and governance, board independence and key-man risk. Moody's cut the outlook last week from positive to stable. Nvidia closed 3.9% lower on 25 Nov. Anthropic fell nearly 10% early, then closed 1.08% higher.

unconfirmed: Headlines say Nasdaq futures rallied and AI stocks rebounded today after a week of wild swings.
Headlines say Treasuries sold off as equities gained, and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are heading for their worst November since 2008.
Headlines mention Gulf attacks and a monthly oil gain; no official oil data after 24 Nov.
driver_reason: Nvidia and the AI trade set the direction of the Nasdaq-100 on 24 and 25 Nov. The S&P credit action and the hot core PCE print added pressure, while yields fell and defensives limited losses.
leader_reason: The Nasdaq-100 trailed the S&P 500 by 0.38 pct pts on 25 Nov and by 2.02 pct pts over five sessions. VXN was 38.53 against VIX 28.29 on 25 Nov, so tech carries the extra risk premium. COR1M at 25.45 is far below the 20 Nov peak, which fits stock-specific AI stress more than broad selling.
